warhead.provenance: No public warhead mass for YJ-12. Engineering-estimate surrogate scaled up from the repo/packet YJ-83K pattern given YJ-12's much larger ~2,500 kg supersonic-ramjet airframe class, comparable to a large supersonic ASCM such as the Russian P-800 Oniks class.

fuze.provenance: No public fuze timing data; engineering-estimate impact/delay fuze scaffold, scaled up from YJ-83K for a large supersonic ASCM.

_real_world.designation: YJ-12 (air-launched baseline); ship-launched YJ-12A and coastal YJ-12B variants also exist
_real_world.role: Supersonic ramjet-powered air-launched anti-ship cruise missile (ASCM), also attributed to J-15 per PRC media
_real_world.carrier_platforms: J-15T (external, per Chinese military media; does not fit internally in J-35 per the OOB doc's LO-loadout table) (csg-cn-yj12-csis-img, csg-cn-yj12-usni-2026, B)
_real_world.dod_system_reach: 3,100-4,000 km for H-6+YJ-12/YJ-83 combined bomber radius (~3,500km) + missile; NOT missile-only (csg-cn-dod-cmpr-2025, A)
_real_world.range_class: Class figure derived by analogy to the ship-launched YJ-12/YJ-18-class 270-290 nmi (~500-537 km) figure cited by USNI (2026) for the broader YJ-12/YJ-18 supersonic ASCM class (csg-cn-yj20-usni-2026, B), though this class figure describes the ship-launched round and may not transfer directly to the air-launched variant, which typically has shorter powered range due to a smaller rocket-boost/ramjet-transition profile when launched at lower altitude/speed than a ballistic-boosted ship-launched round
_real_world.propulsion: Supersonic ramjet-sustained cruise (well-established public characterization for the YJ-12 family)
_real_world.status: content_only_no_mechanism (air-launch spawns a generic missile per authoring_standard; no functional NavalWeaponType anti-ship mount exists yet in the engine mechanism set)

warhead.type.note: blast_fragmentation is the standard ASCM warhead family assumed following the repo's harpoon_ship.json/YJ-83K pattern; no PLAN source describes detonation mechanism

mass_kg.note: no public mass figure for YJ-12; engineering-estimate scaled to the large supersonic-ramjet ASCM class (comparable to the ~3,000 kg P-800 Oniks/BrahMos class, sized down slightly given YJ-12's smaller reported ~200mm booster diameter class), reflecting a large external-carriage air-launched round consistent with the OOB doc noting it does not fit internally in J-35

max_flight_time_s.note: engineering estimate derived from the sourced ~270-290 nmi (~500-537 km) class figure for the broader YJ-12/YJ-18 supersonic ASCM family (USNI 2026, B) at the estimated Mach 2.5 supersonic ramjet-sustained cruise speed; this class figure describes the ship-launched round and may overstate the air-launched variant's practical range, flagged as a proxy risk

flight_model.max_speed.note: Mach 2.5: no specific public number for YJ-12's cruise speed, but supersonic ramjet propulsion is a well-established public characterization for this missile family; Mach 2.5 is a representative mid-range estimate for a ramjet-sustained ASCM (comparable Western/Russian analogs cruise Mach 2-3)

flight_model.max_g.note: no public maneuver-load figure; engineering estimate for a large supersonic sea-skimming ASCM, lower agility than a smaller subsonic missile given the larger airframe mass

flight_model.max_turn_rate.note: no public figure; engineering estimate consistent with max_g

modeling_notes: Per the OOB doc's J-35 loadout table (line 142): YJ-83K and YJ-12 'do not fit internally' in J-35's weapons bay; carrying them is external and non-LO. This record is therefore wired only into J-15T's external default_loadout, not J-35's, per the task's requirement that J-35's internal-vs-external carriage follow the page.
No functional mount exists for air-launched ASCMs of this class (mechanism gap, same as YJ-83K/YJ-18A/YJ-20); content-only. Air-launch path still spawns a generic missile per authoring_standard.
